description: These endpoints deliver the public warnings shown in Germany's official NINA warning app, bringing together alerts from civil protection, weather, flood and police systems in one machine-readable feed. They are operated by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK), which runs the modular warning system MoWaS. Coverage is Germany, with separate lists for MoWaS, the KATWARN and BIWAPP apps, the German Weather Service, state flood centres and police. Each list gives current warnings with identifier, start time, severity, urgency and multilingual titles, and each warning can be fetched as a document following the Common Alerting Protocol structure, with headline, description, instructions, event codes and affected areas; a dashboard endpoint returns warnings for an official regional key. The feeds are free and available without registration as JSON, but the provider publishes no documentation or bulk download and no licence on the endpoints, and only current warnings are returned. Caveats: the interface is undocumented and may change, historical warnings are not archived here, and area geometries must be requested separately. Simulation uses: feeding live alerts into emergency response dashboards and digital twins, and collecting a warning archive to study alert timing and reach. Related records: the WMO Register of Alerting Authorities (data-wmo-register-of-alerting-authorities) lists issuers worldwide, and the US National Weather Service alerts (data-nws-cap-alerts) are a documented CAP counterpart.
